predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Lesbos, given to Francesco I Gattilusio as the dowry of John V's sister Maria Palaiologina

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Lesbos, 'captured by an Ottoman fleet in September 1462', ending the family's power

ledger.x: 17 July 1355: John V Palaiologos makes Francesco Gattilusio lord of Lesbos.
About 1453: Dorino I Gattilusio receives Lemnos as a fief 'shortly before the Fall of Constantinople in 1453'.
1456: the Ottomans take the north Aegean islands.
January 1456: Ainos surrenders to Mehmed II.
September 1462: the Ottoman fleet takes Lesbos.
September 1462: the Gattilusi lordship ends after 107 years.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Gattilusi north Aegean (1456)
wars.outcome: Ainos surrendered in January 1456; the Ottomans removed the Gattilusi from all their lands except Lesbos, which they kept for an annual payment of 4,000 gold pieces.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Lesbos
wars.outcome: An Ottoman fleet captured Lesbos in September 1462; Niccolo Gattilusio was taken to Constantinople.

certainty.note: Islands and a Thracian port town: coasts are the border.
